input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct validation campaign for vLLM ROCm serving parity

## Description

Runs a validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct accelerators to establish
first-hand functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the
platform's supported model set, and produces the per-model go/no-go scope that
determines which models the ROCm serving runtime productization covers. This is
the strategy's risk-reduction gate: the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds
today and has no first-hand ROCm parity data for its supported models.

## Scope

- Secure access to dedicated AMD Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab
  engagement; the access path is unresolved at strategy sign-off and resolving
  it is part of this epic's work.
- Define the campaign methodology: functional correctness checks and
  performance parity measurements versus the CUDA baseline for each model in
  the supported model set, with explicit pass/fail criteria per model.
- Stand up the vLLM ROCm serving stack on the acquired hardware using upstream
  ROCm runtime images.
- Execute the campaign across the supported model set, including multi-GPU
  serving configurations where applicable.
- Deliver a campaign report: per-model functional results, performance parity
  data, and a per-model go/no-go recommendation that constitutes the
  productization scope handed to downstream productization work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The campaign report records functional validation results (pass/fail) for
  every model in the supported model set, measured on physical AMD Instinct
  hardware.
- The campaign report records performance parity measurements against the CUDA
  baseline for every model in the supported model set.
- Every model carries an explicit go/no-go recommendation with the criteria
  used, and the aggregate constitutes the productization scope handed to the
  serving runtime productization work.
- The methodology (parity criteria, measurement procedure, hardware and software
  configuration) is documented in the report so the results are reproducible.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): a validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware
  establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the
  supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization.

## Risks / Notes

- Hardware access (procurement vs. partner lab) is unresolved and externally
  controlled. This epic's work includes securing access, but the access being
  granted is an availability precondition, not an acceptance criterion — the
  deliverable this epic is judged on is the validated report.
- Upstream ROCm runtime image releases are controlled by AMD and the upstream
  communities; the campaign runs against the available upstream images and is
  not blocked by release-train alignment.
- The campaign is likely larger than one sprint of effort (functional plus
  performance parity across the full supported model set on shared hardware);
  it is kept as one logical change because a split would duplicate hardware
  environment bring-up and fragment a single go/no-go report. Re-split into
  sequential waves by model family if the campaign exceeds two sprints.

# Productize the vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

Builds and productizes a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models
cleared by the validation campaign — the platform's first supported AMD
accelerator serving runtime, extending the existing CUDA-only productized
runtime family. Scope is defined by the campaign's go/no-go report: only the
models it clears are productized.

## Scope

- Build the vLLM ROCm runtime container image in the existing midstream vLLM
  repository, based on upstream ROCm builds.
- Define and productize the ServingRuntime (or ClusterServingRuntime) for the
  ROCm variant so it can be selected for KServe InferenceServices, including
  amd.com/gpu resource handling and node placement on AMD Instinct nodes.
- Validate the productized runtime end-to-end under KServe InferenceServices
  on AMD Instinct hardware for the cleared model set. This covers the KServe
  component of the strategy, which requires no code changes: InferenceServices
  must schedule and serve correctly with the ROCm runtime and amd.com/gpu
  resources.
- Release enablement for the cleared model list, including the supported model
  list record for the ROCm runtime.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A vLLM ROCm serving runtime image is built in the midstream repository and
  released green through the platform's Konflux build pipeline (the ROCm image
  variant included).
- The runtime is deployable as a ServingRuntime under KServe InferenceServices
  with amd.com/gpu resources on AMD Instinct nodes.
- Every model on the validation campaign's cleared list serves successfully
  (functional correctness) through the productized runtime on AMD Instinct
  hardware.
- The supported/validated model list recorded for the ROCm runtime matches the
  campaign's go/no-go scope.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the
  models the validation campaign clears.

## Risks / Notes

- Scope is defined by the validation campaign's go/no-go report: a reduced
  cleared list reduces scope; a full no-go removes the productization in favor
  of handing off the campaign findings.
- Upstream ROCm image release cadence may not align with platform release
  trains (externally controlled by AMD and the upstream communities); pin to
  the nearest aligned upstream build and record the deviation.

# Konflux build pipeline for the vLLM ROCm runtime image

## Description

Extends the existing Konflux onboarding of the midstream vLLM repository with
the build pipeline recipe for the new ROCm runtime image variant, so the image
is built, tested, and released through the platform's standard pipeline with
the same release artifacts as the CUDA variants. This is known-recipe pipeline
work for a new container image in an already-onboarded repository, and it runs
in parallel with the runtime image build and productization work — the coupling
(the ROCm image being released green through this pipeline) is expressed as an
acceptance criterion on that work, not as a dependency.

## Scope

- Add the ROCm image variant to the repository's Konflux build configuration.
- Configure the build and test tasks applicable to the ROCm variant.
- Verify the pipeline produces the ROCm image with the expected provenance and
  attestations, matching the existing CUDA variant's pipeline outputs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Konflux pipeline builds the vLLM ROCm runtime image variant and completes
  green.
- The image is produced with the standard release artifacts (signed
  attestations/provenance) matching the existing CUDA variant's pipeline
  outputs.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the
  cleared models — this epic delivers its build/release pipeline aspect.

## Risks / Notes

- Proceeds in parallel with the validation campaign and the runtime
  productization; it is outcome-independent known-recipe work, but its value is
  contingent on the campaign clearing at least some models.

# PyTorch training on ROCm via PyTorchJob

## Description

Enables PyTorch training on AMD Instinct accelerators for single- and
multi-GPU jobs submitted as PyTorchJobs, using ROCm-based PyTorch execution
environments. This is the Training Operator side of the strategy's training
requirement; queueing and quota handling for these jobs is tracked separately
under Distributed Workloads and coordinated via acceptance criteria rather than
a dependency.

## Scope

- Support PyTorchJob execution on AMD GPU nodes with ROCm PyTorch images,
  including worker pods that request amd.com/gpu resources.
- Validate single-GPU and multi-GPU (multi-worker) PyTorchJob topologies on
  AMD Instinct hardware.
- Validate compatible upstream ROCm PyTorch image usage for training jobs and
  record the compatible image guidance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob using a ROCm PyTorch image completes training
  successfully on AMD Instinct nodes.
- A multi-GPU (distributed, multi-worker) PyTorchJob completes training
  successfully on AMD Instinct nodes.
- Jobs correctly request and receive amd.com/gpu resources on AMD GPU nodes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU
  jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling — this epic
  covers the PyTorchJob execution side.

## Risks / Notes

- Requires AMD Instinct hardware for validation; hardware access is secured
  through the validation campaign's procurement/partner-lab engagement, so
  scheduling must be coordinated (coordination risk, not a dependency).
- Upstream ROCm PyTorch image release cadence is controlled by AMD and the
  upstream communities; image availability may not align with platform release
  trains.

# Kueue admission and amd.com/gpu quota for ROCm training workloads

## Description

Ensures PyTorchJob training workloads on AMD accelerators are admitted through
Kueue with correct amd.com/gpu quota accounting — extending the platform's
existing queueing and quota machinery to the AMD resource name. This is the
Distributed Workloads side of the strategy's training requirement; the
PyTorchJob execution enablement is tracked separately under the Training
Operator and coordinated via acceptance criteria rather than a dependency,
since quota configuration is a configuration reference between the two.

## Scope

- Support amd.com/gpu resource quota handling in Kueue ClusterQueue/LocalQueue
  quota accounting for accelerated queues.
- Ensure single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJobs on ROCm are admitted through Kueue,
  including all-or-nothing (gang) admission for multi-worker jobs.
- Validate quota accounting: admitted workloads' amd.com/gpu usage is correctly
  charged while running and released on completion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A ROCm PyTorchJob requesting amd.com/gpu is admitted through a Kueue queue
  whose quota is configured for amd.com/gpu.
- Multi-worker (gang) admission holds for multi-GPU ROCm jobs: a workload is
  admitted only when all its pods' amd.com/gpu requests can be satisfied.
- Quota is correctly accounted while jobs run and released on completion.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU
  jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling — this epic
  covers the admission and quota side.

## Risks / Notes

- Requires AMD Instinct hardware for end-to-end admission validation;
  scheduling must be coordinated with the validation campaign's hardware
  access (coordination risk, not a dependency).

# AMD ROCm enablement documentation

## Description

Documents the AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training: the supported
AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list established by
the validation campaign and the productized runtime. Goes through the Red Hat
docs content process and is written after the implementation work it describes.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Supported AMD Instinct hardware (accelerator models) for vLLM serving and
  PyTorch training.
- Driver prerequisites for AMD GPU nodes (stated as prerequisites; the platform
  does not provision drivers).
- The validated model list for the vLLM ROCm serving runtime, matching the
  campaign's cleared list and the productized runtime's supported model list.
- Setup and configuration guidance: selecting the ROCm serving runtime under
  KServe InferenceServices, and Kueue quota configuration for amd.com/gpu
  training jobs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the supported AMD hardware, the driver
  prerequisites, and the validated model list.
- The documented validated model list matches the productized ROCm serving
  runtime's supported model list.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented serving
  runtime, training, and queueing behavior, with review sign-off recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver
  prerequisites, and the validated model list.

## Risks / Notes

- Content depends on the validation campaign's outcome: a reduced cleared list
  rewrites the validated-model-list topic; a full no-go replaces the serving
  content with a statement of unsupported status.
